text: Dana, a fulfiller holding the itil role, opens a ticket. She can open Incidents assigned to her team just fine, and she can edit most fields, but she can't change the Assignment group field, it's greyed out, and it worked for her on other tickets just last month. Let's work this exactly the way the previous lesson's order of operations laid out, step by step.

First, classify it. Dana can open the record and edit most fields, so the table-level write ACL is clearly passing, because if it weren't, she couldn't edit anything on the record at all. The symptom is isolated to one specific field, which points straight at a field-level ACL named incident.assignment_group, exactly the table-level-versus-field-level pattern from earlier in this chapter.

Next, reproduce it with the Security Debugger rather than guessing. Impersonating Dana or having her reload the same Incident with the debugger active shows incident.write passing on her itil role, and then, lower in the trace, incident.assignment_group failing on the write operation specifically, which matches exactly what she described.

Opening that failing ACL shows no role requirement at all and no condition, just a script that checks whether the current user is a member of whichever group currently sits in the record's assignment group field, setting answer true only if they are. Dana's itil role is completely irrelevant to this particular ACL.

That explains everything. Last month's ticket happened to be assigned to Dana's own group, so the script passed. This ticket is assigned to a different group she isn't a member of, so it now fails, with absolutely no change to her role at all. Confirming her actual group memberships against the record's real assignment group, rather than trusting memory of how it worked before, verifies the script is behaving correctly. If that's the real intended business rule, no fix is needed, just explain the behavior and have her request reassignment through her team lead instead. If the requirement has genuinely changed, that's when editing the script, with Elevate Roles turned on first, actually becomes necessary.
